name: Bitcoin Gold
classificationNote: Upstream label "Bridge & Cross-Chain / Forged Proof" on a base-layer chain: reclassified as a 51%/consensus attack.
rootCause: Bitcoin Gold was 51% attacked by an unknown attacker. This type of attack allows an attacker to manipulate the blockchain ledger that records transactions. During the attack, 388,000 BTG (worth approximately US$18 million) was stolen from several cryptocurrency exchanges. After the team refused to help pay for some of the losses, Bitcoin Gold was subsequently delisted from Bittrex.

descriptions.text: Bitcoin Gold was 51% attacked by an unknown attacker. This type of attack allows an attacker to manipulate the blockchain ledger that records transactions. During the attack, 388,000 BTG (worth approximately US$18 million) was stolen from several cryptocurrency exchanges. After the team refused to help pay for some of the losses, Bitcoin Gold was subsequently delisted from Bittrex.

Bitcoin Gold suffered a coordinated 51% attack in May 2018, enabling the attacker to double-spend over 388,000 BTG ($18 million) at exchanges by manipulating the chain and withdrawing funds from fraudulent deposits before detection. The root cause was a low total network hashrate combined with the Equihash (Zhash) mining algorithm, which allowed the attacker to rent or coordinate enough hashpower to consistently control more than 50% of the Bitcoin Gold network. This enabled deep chain reorganizations and double-spend attacks targeting exchanges.
